2.2.1 GENERAL INTRODUCTION Fungus (latin; fungour- to flourish) are non-green, nucleated, non-vascular thallophytes. They are eukaryotic organisms and include yeasts, moulds and mushrooms. The branch of Botany that deals with fungi is called mycology. The scientist who is concerned with fungi is called mycologist.

They grow in diverse habitats i.e. found in almost every available habitat on earth where organic material is present. They occur in air, water, soil and on animals and plants. They prefer to grow in warm and humid places. Fungi are multicellular except yeast. Except yeast, the body of fungus is made up of long, slender thread like structures called hyphae. The network of hyphae is known as mycelium. Some hyphae are continuous tubes filled with multinucleated cytoplasm called as coenocytic hyphae while other have septa or cross walls in their hyphae. The cell wall is of fungi is made up of chitin.

Fungi are heterotrophic and absorb soluble organic matter from dead substrates and hence are called saprophytes. Some are parasites (e.g. Fusarium). They can also live as symbionts-in association with algae as lichens and with roots of higher plants as mycorrhiza. Reproduction in fungi takes place by vegetative, asexual and sexual method.

2.2.2 CLASSIFICATION On the basis of morphology of the mycelium, mode of spore formation and fruiting bodies Kingdom Mycota is classified into various classes.
1. Phycomycetes (The algal fungi) Characteristics features of phycomycetes are as follows:
a. They are found in aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in moist and damp places or as obligate parasites on plants.
b. Thallus is mycelium. The mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic. c. Asexual reproduction takes place by the formation of spores which are produced

inside sporangium. Terrestrial species produced aplanospores and aquatic species produced zoospores. d. The zoospores may be uniflagellate or biflagellate. e. The sexual reproduction may be isogamous or oogamous.
The class Phycomycetes is further classified into sub-classes, oomycetes and zygomycetes.
